verdict: Alphabet's revenue rose 18% to $113.8B as Google Cloud surged 48%, and annual revenue passed $400B for the first time — though a $2.1B Waymo pay charge sat inside the quarter's costs.

segments.name: Google Services
segments.note: Search, YouTube, subscriptions and devices. Search revenue grew 17%, subscriptions, platforms and devices 17%, and YouTube ads 9%; YouTube's ads-plus-subscriptions revenue passed $60B for the full year.

segments.name: Google Cloud
segments.note: Cloud computing for businesses — growth accelerated to 48% on enterprise AI infrastructure and AI solutions, and Cloud ended 2025 at an annual run rate over $70B.

segments.name: Other Bets
segments.note: Moonshot projects like Waymo self-driving cars; they lost $3.6B at the operating level, including a $2.1B employee compensation charge.

segments.name: Hedging losses
segments.note: Losses on Alphabet's currency-hedging program, which exists to smooth out exchange-rate swings on its overseas revenue.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Engineers and AI research; up 42% YoY, including the $2.1B Waymo employee compensation charge.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling ads and cloud contracts, and marketing Google's products.

otherDetail: A net gain of $3,183M, including a $2.3B net gain on equity securities — stakes Alphabet holds in other companies.
follow100Note: The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Cloud is surging
takeaways.text: Google Cloud revenue jumped 48% to $17.7B and its operating profit more than doubled to $5.3B. Cloud ended 2025 at an annual run rate above $70B, driven by enterprise AI demand.

takeaways.title: A Waymo pay charge sat in the costs
takeaways.text: Operating income includes a $2.1B employee compensation charge for Waymo, based on its estimated stock valuation and recorded mostly in R&D. Operating income still rose 16% to $35.9B.

takeaways.title: A $400 billion year
takeaways.text: Full-year 2025 revenue was $402.8B — the first time Alphabet has passed $400B. Paid subscriptions passed 325 million, and 2026 capex is planned at $175-185B to keep up with AI demand.

oneTimers: Operating income includes a $2.1B employee compensation charge for Waymo, based on estimated stock valuation, primarily reflected in research and development expenses.
Other income includes a $2.3B net gain on equity securities (stakes Alphabet holds in other companies), which added $1.8B to net income after tax.
